answer: In an agent economy, each identity must lock a refundable stake before voting, and the contract counts at most one vote per stake. Agents named walnut, cipher, and sable can all participate, but an attacker creating a thousand identities must lock a thousand stakes for the full voting period. The deposit does not prove identities are distinct; it makes multiplying them capital-intensive and exposes the attacker to the opportunity cost of immobilized funds.
